2021_179_8_a_bond_authorizing_resolution.paragraph: A bond authorizing resolution before the Troy School District Board of Education, County of Oakland, Michigan, at a regular meeting conducted electronically on March 16, 2021 at 7:00 p.m. It authorizes “2021 Refunding Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation) (Taxable)” in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed Forty-Five Million Dollars ($45,000,000) to advance refund callable maturities of the District’s 2012 Refunding Bonds, dated December 20, 2012, and 2014 School Building and Site Bonds, dated January 29, 2014. The governing parameter is that net present value savings must equal at least one percent (1.00%) of projected debt service on the refunded bonds, with interest not exceeding four percent (4.00%) per annum.
2021_179_8_a_bond_authorizing_resolution.page:
**Instrument and setting**
Resolution Authorizing 2021 Refunding Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation) (Taxable), Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, offered at a regular meeting of the Board of Education conducted electronically on March 16, 2021 at 7:00 p.m., prevailing Eastern Time. Mover, supporter, present/absent members, and AYES/NAYS are blank in the draft; the certification is signed by Gary Hauff, Secretary, Board of Education, citing the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.

**Purpose**
Authority to refund comes from Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001, as amended (the Revised Municipal Finance Act). The Prior Bonds are the 2012 Refunding Bonds (General Obligation – Unlimited Tax), dated December 20, 2012, and the 2014 School Building and Site Bonds (General Obligation – Unlimited Tax), dated January 29, 2014. The Municipal Advisor advised that net present value savings of debt service costs may be achievable; the refunding is structured on a taxable basis.

**Authorized parameters**
| Item | Parameter |
| --- | --- |
| Maximum aggregate principal | $45,000,000 |
| Denomination | $5,000 or integral multiples |
| Maximum interest rate | 4.00% per annum |
| Interest payment dates | May 1 and November 1, semi-annually |
| Maturity | May 1 of years fixed at sale |
| Minimum net present value savings | 1.00% of projected debt service on the Refunded Bonds |
| Sale price range | not less than 99%, not more than 105% of par |

Final terms are delegated to the Superintendent and the Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, either acting individually as an “Authorized Officer,” under Section 315(1)(d) of the Act.

**Funds and security**
Commencing with the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2020, the District must levy annually a tax sufficient to pay principal and interest, without limitation as to rate or amount, under Article IX, Sections 6 and 16 of the Michigan Constitution of 1963. A 2021 Refunding Bonds Debt Retirement Fund is opened unless a Common Debt Retirement Fund exists. Proceeds first fund a 2021 Refunding Bonds Costs of Issuance Fund, with any surplus moved to the Debt Retirement Fund; the balance goes to an Escrow Fund held by an Escrow Agent under an Escrow Agreement, invested in United States obligations to pay the Refunded Bonds.

**Sale mechanics**
Competitive public sale is the default, with a Notice of Sale published in the Bond Buyer, New York, New York, and award to the lowest true interest cost. Paragraph 11 permits a negotiated sale instead: a public offering through a selected senior Underwriter, or a private placement with a qualified bank or sophisticated institutional investor through a Placement Agent, in which case no continuing disclosure undertaking is required and the bonds may be exempt from the rating requirement of Section 323 of the Act.

**Professionals**
Bond Counsel: Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. Municipal Advisor: PFM Financial Advisors LLC, 555 Briarwood Circle, Suite 333, Ann Arbor, Michigan 48108, (734) 994-9700, facsimile (734) 994-9710.

**Notice of Sale maturity schedule (Exhibit B)**
| Year | Amount | Year | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2022 | $3,545,000 | 2026 | $5,465,000 |
| 2023 | $8,040,000 | 2027 | $6,730,000 |
| 2024 | $5,895,000 | 2028 | $6,790,000 |
| 2025 | $5,510,000 | | |

**Exhibits**
A – Bond Form; B – Notice of Sale, signed Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent; C – Continuing Disclosure Undertaking under SEC Rule 15c2-12; D – Purchaser Certificate for a private placement; E – Final Qualification Application under Act 92, Public Acts of Michigan, 2005.
2021_179_8_a_bond_authorizing_resolution.verbose:
**Identification**
Resolution Authorizing 2021 Refunding Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation) (Taxable), Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan. Minutes recite a regular meeting of the Board of Education conducted electronically on March 16, 2021, at 7:00 p.m., prevailing Eastern Time. Mover, supporter, PRESENT and ABSENT members, and the AYES and NAYS lists are blank. Gary Hauff, Secretary, Board of Education, signs both the adoption block and the certification that notice complied with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976. Reference numbers 37318682 and 37318682.1/091101.00049 appear.

**Recitals**
Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001, as amended, the Revised Municipal Finance Act, permits refunding of funded indebtedness. The Prior Bonds are the 2012 Refunding Bonds (General Obligation – Unlimited Tax), dated December 20, 2012, and the 2014 School Building and Site Bonds (General Obligation – Unlimited Tax), dated January 29, 2014. The Municipal Advisor advised net present value savings of debt service costs may be accomplished. The Board determines it is in the District’s best interest to issue bonds not to exceed Forty-Five Million Dollars ($45,000,000) to advance refund all or a portion of the callable maturities of the Prior Bonds (the “Refunded Bonds”) on a taxable basis, and notes the District must be qualified or obtain prior approval from the Michigan Department of Treasury.

**Bond authorization and details (paragraphs 1–2)**
Bonds may be issued in one or more series, not exceeding $45,000,000 or such lesser amount as determined by the Superintendent and the Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, either acting individually (each an “Authorized Officer”). Bonds are registered as to principal and interest in the denomination of $5,000 or integral multiples, dated as of delivery, numbered by the Transfer Agent, maturing May 1 in years and amounts set at sale. Interest may not exceed four percent (4.00%) per annum, payable semi-annually on May 1 and November 1, provided net present value savings are not less than one percent (1.00%) of projected debt service on the Refunded Bonds absent the refunding, based on Treasury guidelines. Sale price must be not less than 99% and not more than 105% of principal. Serial or term bonds are permitted; term bonds designated by the original purchaser carry mandatory redemption per the Notice of Sale schedule. Interest is paid by check mailed to the registered owner of record as of the fifteenth day of the month prior to the payment date. Book-entry-only issuance through The Depository Trust Company, New York, New York, is permitted.

**Execution, tax levy, funds, proceeds (paragraphs 3–6)**
Bonds follow Exhibit A, signed by manual or facsimile signatures of the President and Secretary of the Board, valid only upon Transfer Agent authentication, delivered per instructions from the Treasurer of the School District. Commencing with the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2020, the District must levy annually a tax sufficient to pay principal and interest when due, without limitation as to rate or amount, as permitted by Article IX, Section 6 and Article IX, Section 16 of the Michigan Constitution of 1963. Unless a Common Debt Retirement Fund exists, the Treasurer opens a 2021 Refunding Bonds Debt Retirement Fund; tax proceeds, accrued interest on delivery, and any net original issue premium are deposited there, and premium may reduce the principal amount issued if federal tax law requires. Proceeds fund a 2021 Refunding Bonds Costs of Issuance Fund, with any surplus transferred to the Debt Retirement Fund; the balance, plus money transferred from the debt retirement fund for the Refunded Bonds, is invested in direct obligations of or obligations unconditionally guaranteed by the United States of America in one or more Escrow Funds held by a bank or trust company as trustee and Escrow Agent under Escrow Agreements irrevocably directing redemption of the specified Prior Bonds.

**Sale, ratings, disclosure, negotiated alternatives (paragraphs 7–12)**
The Authorized Officer may fix a sale date, publish notice in the Bond Buyer, New York, New York, in the form of Exhibit B, award to the bidder producing the lowest true interest cost, and execute a sale order without further Board direction. Bond ratings and municipal bond insurance may be pursued if deemed appropriate by the Municipal Advisor and Bond Counsel. The District covenants under SEC Rule 15c2-12 to provide the Exhibit C information. A negotiated sale is permitted: a public offering with a selected senior Underwriter and optional co-managing underwriters, or a private placement with a qualified bank or sophisticated institutional investor (the “Purchaser”) via a Placement Agent, with an Exhibit D certificate, no continuing disclosure undertaking, possible exemption from the rating requirement of Section 323 of the Act, and a private placement memorandum in lieu of the Official Statement. Final details may be adjusted under Section 315(1)(d) of the Act.

**Professionals, Treasury, further actions (paragraphs 13–17)**
Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. is appointed Bond Counsel; PFM Financial Advisors LLC is appointed Municipal Advisor. Treasury waivers, including rating waivers, and a Security Report are authorized, as is qualification under the School Bond Qualification, Approval, and Loan Act, Act 92, Public Acts of Michigan, 2005, as amended, with the Secretary directed to submit the Application for Final Qualification in the form of Exhibit E. Payable costs of issuance include Bond Counsel fees, Municipal Advisor fees, rating agency fees, Transfer Agent fees, Escrow Agent fees, and official statement printing. Conflicting resolutions are rescinded.

**Exhibit A – Bond Form**
Interest is computed on a 360-day year of twelve 30-day months, first payable in 2021 and semiannually thereafter, maturing May 1. The bond recites Act 451, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, as amended, Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001, as amended, and the resolution adopted March 16, 2021; pledges full faith, credit and resources; states bonds are not subject to optional redemption prior to maturity; requires sixty (60) days’ mailed notice of a Transfer Agent change; and sets the record date at the fifteenth (15th) day of the month.

**Exhibit B – Form of Notice of Sale**
Electronic bids may go to the Municipal Advisory Council of Michigan at munibids@macmi.com and to Bidcomp/Parity, contact Anthony Leyden or CLIENT SERVICES, 1359 Broadway, Second Floor, New York, New York 10018, (212) 849-5021. Bonds are $5,000 denominations with interest payable November 1, 2021 and semiannually thereafter. Maturities on May 1: 2022, $3,545,000; 2023, $8,040,000; 2024, $5,895,000; 2025, $5,510,000; 2026, $5,465,000; 2027, $6,730,000; 2028, $6,790,000. The District may adjust the aggregate after bids in increments of $5,000 in any maturity, not exceeding $45,000,000, with proportional purchase price adjustment and unchanged bid rates. Rates may not exceed four percent (4%) per annum, expressed in multiples of 1/8 or 1/100 of 1%, uniform within a maturity year, with a spread between highest and lowest rates bid of not more than two percent (2%). No bid for less than all bonds or at less than 99% or more than 105% of par is considered. There is no optional redemption; a term bond option allows mandatory redemption on May 1 at par plus accrued interest, selected by lot. Bonds are book-entry only, registered to Cede & Co. for The Depository Trust Company. Purpose is refunding a portion of the outstanding 2012 Refunding Bonds dated December 20, 2012 and the 2014 School Building and Site Bonds dated January 29, 2014 plus issuance costs, as a full faith and credit unlimited tax general obligation payable from ad valorem taxes. The bonds are expected to be fully qualified under Act 92, Public Acts of Michigan, 2005, under which the State of Michigan would lend the District amounts sufficient to pay principal and interest. A good faith deposit of one percent (1%) of the final aggregate principal amount, payable to the Treasurer of the School District, is due by Noon, prevailing Eastern Time, the next business day after sale, bears no interest, and is forfeited if the bid is not honored. Award is on lowest true interest cost, compounded November 1, 2021 and semiannually. The legal opinion is by Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C., Detroit, Michigan, with fees paid from bond proceeds. Interest is not excludable from gross income for federal income tax purposes under the Internal Revenue Service Code of 1986, as amended. If bonds are not tendered by Noon on the 45th day following the sale date, the bidder may withdraw and the deposit is returned. Continuing disclosure begins with the fiscal year ending June 30, 2021, due on or prior to the last day of the sixth month after fiscal year end. Bond insurance is at the purchaser’s option and expense, though the District pays for any rating it requested. CUSIP application is made by PFM Financial Advisors LLC; printing is paid by the District and the CUSIP Service Bureau assignment charge by the purchaser. The final Official Statement is delivered electronically within 7 business days of sale, with copy requests within 24 hours. Bidders certify they are not an “Iran-Linked Business” under Act 517, Public Acts of Michigan, 2012, MCL 129.311 et seq. Municipal Advisor contact: PFM Financial Advisors LLC, 555 Briarwood Circle, Suite 333, Ann Arbor, Michigan, 48108, (734) 994-9700, facsimile (734) 994-9710. Signed by Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent, Troy School District.

**Exhibit C – Form of Continuing Disclosure Undertaking**
Definitions include Audited Financial Statements required by Act 2, Public Acts of Michigan, 1968, as amended; EMMA, the MSRB’s Electronic Municipal Market Access system; Financial Obligation; and the Rule, SEC Rule 15c2-12 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Filings through EMMA commence with the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021 and update Official Statement tables: ENROLLMENT – Historical Enrollment; STATE AID PAYMENTS; PROPERTY VALUATIONS – History of Valuations; MAJOR TAXPAYERS; SCHOOL DISTRICT TAX RATES (per $1,000 of Valuation); TAX LEVIES AND COLLECTIONS; RETIREMENT PLAN – Contribution to MPSERS; DEBT STATEMENT – DIRECT DEBT; SCHOOL LOAN REVOLVING FUND (SLRF) PROGRAM; and GENERAL FUND BUDGET SUMMARY in Appendix C. Sixteen listed events require notice within ten business days, including payment delinquencies, unscheduled draws on debt service reserves, adverse tax opinions and IRS Form 5701-TEB Notices of Proposed Issue, bond calls, defeasances, rating changes, bankruptcy, mergers, trustee changes, and Financial Obligation defaults. Enforcement is limited to specific performance, and noncompliance is not a default on the Bonds.

**Exhibits D and E**
Exhibit D is a Purchaser Certificate for a private placement: the Purchaser certifies it is an “accredited investor” under Regulation D of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, is not relying on representations of the District or Bond Counsel, and understands the bonds are unregistered under the Securities Act of 1933 and the Michigan Uniform Securities Act, unlisted, unrated, and possibly not readily marketable. The bonds bear a legend restricting resale to registered or exempt transactions. Exhibit E is the Form of Final Qualification Application, pages E-1 through E-4.
